newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Friday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but profit-taking pushed prices off their highs, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 21,530 yuan ($2,595) per tonne, rising 60 yuan. It opened at 21,790 and hit a high of 21,800.
January rose 50 to 20,850, February 90 to 21,010, March 70 to 21,260, May 90 to 21,660, June 100 to 21,700 and July 320 to 21,800.
Combined volume rose to 76,770 tonnes from 25,560.
Copper opened sharply higher due to heavy overnight gains on the LME but profit-taking then pushed prices steadily down during the rest of the session.
"Many investors preferred to take profits given the holiday mood," one trader said. "Copper's movements today will reduce the confidence of long position holders in the next few days."
But some traders said any further rises on the LME would help to boost Shanghai's market sentiment.
"Shanghai copper is likely to rise further depending on the LME's trend in the next few days," a second tarder said. "But it will meet strong resistance around the 21,800-yuan level."
Aluminium ended mostly up. Janaury rose 170 to 14,700 yuan per tonne, February 190 to 15,000, March 100 to 15,310 but April fell 100 to 15,550.
Combined volume rose to 8,480 tonnes from 3,040.
